beats.text: Every named US hurricane was a woman.
beats.note: From 1953, when the US dropped a phonetic-alphabet naming scheme for storms, until 1979, hurricanes and tropical storms got female names only. No exceptions.

beats.text: Storms got described the way lazy jokes describe women.
beats.note: Forecasters called them 'temperamental', said they were 'flirting' with the coast. It was treated as charming. Female meteorologists were not charmed.

beats.name: Roxcy Bolton
beats.role: Florida feminist who founded the United States' first rape treatment centre and led the campaign to end female-only hurricane names, arguing that women 'deeply resent being arbitrarily associated with disaster'.

beats.note: The Eastern Pacific added male names first; the Atlantic and Gulf followed the next year. Some forecasters warned male-named storms would not be taken seriously.

beats.text: A later study found the opposite: people underestimate female-named hurricanes, and it has cost lives.

beats.line: The storm never cared what it was called. People did.
